sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Lesson 11.5: Weak Supervision: Foundations and Programmatic Labeling. Having mastered human-in-the-loop active querying in Lessons 11.2 through 11.4, we now explore a paradigm shift known as Software 2.0 Data Programming.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Instead of spending months hand-labeling hundreds of thousands of instances one by one, domain experts write executable Labeling Functions—capturing regexes, knowledge bases, ontologies, and zero-shot prompts—and let unsupervised generative models reconcile noise into probabilistic soft labels.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Let us trace the four-stage Weak Supervision pipeline. Domain experts author multi-source Labeling Functions wrapping regexes, distant knowledge bases like Wikidata, and zero-shot prompts. Evaluating them across unlabeled data produces the Sparse Label Matrix Lambda.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Critically, a Labeling Function is allowed to abstain by returning zero. Unlike a classical classifier that forces a guess on every sample, an LF fires only when its pattern is triggered—allowing unsupervised factor graphs to infer rule accuracy and train deep end models that generalize beyond the rules themselves.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Definition 11.5.1 formalizes the Sparse Label Matrix Lambda. Evaluating an ensemble of m labeling functions across n unlabeled instances generates an n-by-m matrix with entries in negative one, zero, or positive one.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: The non-zero entries induce the binary empirical support mask S, where S i j equals 1 whenever labeling function j abstains not on instance i. While each individual column is highly sparse—covering one to forty percent—their ensemble union spans the vast majority of the unlabeled dataset.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Definition 11.5.2 establishes the telemetry metrics of the sparse label matrix. Individual coverage measures the non-zero fraction in column j, while total pipeline coverage tracks instances covered by at least one rule.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Two pairwise matrices unlock unsupervised accuracy estimation: the Overlap matrix O j k, counting where rules j and k both vote, and the Conflict matrix C j k, counting where they vote with opposing signs. Far from being a nuisance, controlled conflict provides the statistical signal needed to infer which rule is accurate!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Definition 11.5.3 specifies the Data Programming generative label model as a Gibbs or Ising factor graph over the observed votes Lambda and latent true label Y. It learns three factor families: theta acc measuring accuracy, theta prop modeling propensity to vote, and theta corr capturing edge correlations between dependent rules.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Because true label Y is latent, we marginalize over Y in plus or minus one and minimize negative log-likelihood purely on unlabeled votes Lambda—or solve closed-form second-order covariance systems like FlyingSquid—to output calibrated soft targets y tilde i in zero to one.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Interactive Lab 1 below: the Sparse Label Matrix and LF Quality Telemetry Studio! Inspect the live N-by-6 matrix heatmap on Canvas 1, showing positive votes in green, negative votes in red, and abstentions in gray.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Adjust Corpus Size N, Noise Rate eta, and Heuristic Correlation rho to observe on Canvas 2 how unsupervised EM infers low accuracy for the overbroad NoisyNeg rule compared to precise regex heuristics.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Time for Active Checkpoint 1 from your monograph's first Self-Assessment! Given one thousand unlabeled instances where LFs 1 and 2 have pairwise overlap O 1 2 equal to zero point two five and disagree forty percent of the time when both vote.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Calculate the dataset-wide conflict rate C 1 2, and explain the covariance triad identity that lets a generative model infer individual accuracies without gold supervision.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Definition 11.5.4 proves why weakly supervised deep models achieve Bayes optimality. Instead of hard pseudo-labels, we minimize noise-aware soft cross-entropy risk L hat soft over probabilistic posteriors y tilde i.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Ratner and colleagues proved that excess true risk is bounded by Rademacher complexity, the label model estimation error epsilon g, uncovered fraction one minus total coverage, and statistical sampling error scaling as O of n to the minus one half.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: A common failure pattern in weak supervision is replacing a generative label model with simple majority voting. If five labeling functions wrap variations of the same keyword list while one independent rule achieves ninety-five percent accuracy, uniform majority voting counts the correlated echo five times.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Modern engines like Snorkel factor graphs and Chen's FlyingSquid closed-form covariance matrix completion neutralize correlation double-counting and weight expert LFs properly, yielding calibrated soft targets instead of brittle binary hard votes.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Now let's examine Interactive Lab 2 below: Generative Posteriors versus Downstream End-Model Convergence! On Canvas 3, contrast the smooth probabilistic S-curve of the generative model against the jagged discrete steps of naive majority voting.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Click Optimize Model EM plus 5 and toggle the aggregation strategy between Snorkel Generative EM, Naive Majority Vote, and Accuracy-Weighted Vote to watch downstream F1-score climb toward the Gold Supervised Bound on Canvas 4.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Time for Active Checkpoint 2 from Self-Assessment 2! An unlabeled document receives votes plus one from LF1, plus one from LF2, and minus one from LF3. Inferred accuracies are a1 equals zero point seven zero, a2 equals zero point six five, and a3 equals zero point nine five under equal priors.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Compute the exact generative posterior probability that Y equals positive one, and explain how it prevents the mistake made by naive majority voting.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Let us examine two transformative industrial deployments. At Google, Snorkel DryBell deployed distributed Apache Spark factor graphs across Knowledge Graph and web extraction services—labeling over ten million instances, cutting turnaround from six months to forty-eight hours, and beating human gold baselines by one point six F1 points.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: At Stanford Medicine, HIPAA prohibits uploading patient records to public crowdsourcing platforms. Researchers combined forty clinical LFs wrapping UMLS ontologies, NegEx negation parsers, and lab biomarkers across one hundred fifty thousand EHR notes and chest radiographs—matching board-certified radiologists at F1 zero point eight eight seven while saving eighty-two point four percent of physician time.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Time for Active Checkpoint 3! An NLP moderation team deploys five regex LFs wrapping the exact same toxic keyword dictionary alongside two independent, high-precision Transformer heuristic rules, then aggregates labels using unweighted majority voting.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: F1 precision collapses on sarcastic edge cases. Identify the statistical pathology occurring inside the label matrix and the architectural fix.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Let us summarize production engineering discipline. Author twenty to fifty diverse LFs spanning orthogonal modalities—regexes, knowledge bases, negation logic, and zero-shot foundation models—never a single brittle rule family.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Always keep a small, clean gold validation set strictly for auditing empirical accuracy and final generalization, never leak it into unsupervised LF weights, and always train a noise-aware discriminative end model rather than deploying raw heuristic rules directly.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Slide 15 presents the Pydantic V2 production suite from your chapter: WeakSupervisionPipeline. Every rule carries frozen LFMetadata for Git provenance, build label matrix compiles N-by-M sparse votes, and fit generative label model runs unsupervised Expectation-Maximization.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Unit assertions strictly verify that abstained neutral documents remain at neutral posterior zero point five zero, overbroad noisy rules receive lower inferred accuracy than precision regexes, and pipeline coverage hits exact target invariants.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: To conclude Lesson 11.5, remember the four Software 2.0 axioms: encode expertise into abstention-capable Labeling Functions, preserve overlap and conflict for accuracy triangulation, resolve noise via covariance-aware generative factor graphs, and train discriminative end models on soft targets.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Review the foundational papers by Ratner, Varma, Bach, Chen, Fries, and Zhang. In Lesson 11.6, we go deeper into generative matrix completion mathematics and latent dependency recovery!
